mainEntity.name: How much does a Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,800, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge significantly more for the same replacement. Used engines are a popular budget alternative, starting from around £400.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of timing chain failure in a Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection of timing chain issues can prevent catastrophic damage to your Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC. Signs include a distinct rattling or ticking noise from the engine, especially on cold starts, illumination of the check engine light with timing correlation error codes, and rough idling or a noticeable loss of engine performance. If you notice these symptoms, get your Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends entirely on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. For older models valued under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement may approach the vehicle's total value, making a used engine or targeted repair more sensible. For well-maintained examples valued over £6,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is a financially sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct R20A engine code, nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, fluid top-up, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the R20A and other Honda CR-V engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The R20A is a naturally aspirated 2.0-litre i-VTEC petrol engine, prioritising long-term reliability and smooth power delivery. Unlike the 1.5 VTEC Turbo or 2.2 i-DTEC diesel variants, it lacks complex turbochargers or DPF systems. This simplicity makes it a highly sought-after, low-maintenance option for high-mileage family use.

historyTimeline.h2: Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 i-VTEC was introduced to the Honda CR-V lineup, it provided a highly reliable, naturally aspirated petrol option known for its smooth power delivery and robust timing chain design, appealing to owners seeking low-maintenance family transport.

milestones.description: R20A1 introduced in the Honda CR-V Mk3 (RE), offering 150 PS with i-VTEC technology for improved fuel efficiency and performance.
R20A continued in the Honda CR-V Mk4 (RM), featuring minor refinements to the engine management system and updated emissions compliance.
Production of the 2.0 i-VTEC in the UK CR-V range was largely phased out in favour of the 1.5 VTEC Turbo and hybrid powertrains, cementing its legacy as a dependable workhorse.

commonProblems.h3: The Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC is widely regarded as one of the most reliable petrol engines in its class. However, as mileage increases, wear on the timing chain and ancillary components can occur. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Wear - Why the Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC Rattles on Startup
problems.rootCause: Over time, the timing chain can stretch, and the hydraulic tensioner may lose pressure, causing a distinct rattling noise during cold starts. If ignored, it can lead to timing correlation errors and potential internal damage.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before valve or piston damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if timing has slipped causing internal engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC (2007-2018) is currently valued between £3,000 and £10,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: For a Honda CR-V 2.0 i-VTEC showing early signs of chain rattle, a preventative timing chain kit replacement is the most financially sensible route. However, if the engine has suffered timing slippage or internal damage, a reconditioned or rebuilt unit is the most reliable long-term solution to preserve the vehicle's value.
